hook.text: In 1700s England, Parliament let landowners fence off shared fields. Millions of peasants lost access.

buildup.text: Open fields were divided, hedged, and consolidated into private farms owned by gentry.

discovery.text: Private ownership allowed experimentation. Enclosed farms could try new crops and methods freely.

twist.text: Displaced rural workers flooded into cities. They became the labor force for the Industrial Revolution.

climax.text: Enclosure boosted food production but destroyed a way of life. Progress came at a brutal human cost.

punchline.text: Fencing the land fed more people—and uprooted millions.

quiz.question: What was the major social consequence of the Enclosure Movement?
options: Displaced rural workers migrated to cities, fueling industrialization
